title: The many-rank matrix-sum equidistribution conjecture
source: Nick Gill, Noam Lifshitz, László Pyber and Endre Szabó, “Initiating the proof of the Liebeck–Nikolov–Shalev conjecture”, arXiv:2408.07800 (2024). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07800), Conjecture 5.5

lanes.final_paper_and_definition_check: final-paper-check-364356-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-364356.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; definitions literal; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For n by n matrices over a finite field with q elements: if prescribed ranks r_1, ..., r_k sum to at least 2n, then for every target matrix the number of k-tuples of matrices of those ranks with that sum is at most 32768 q^(-n^2) times the product of the sizes of the rank classes. The constant is uniform in q, n, k and the ranks. With all ranks at least epsilon n and k at least ceil(2/epsilon) this proves Conjecture 5.5 of Gill, Lifshitz, Pyber and Szabo in its upper-bound (O(1)) reading; a two-sided reading is false already over F_2 with n = 1. The source proves the case of three summands of rank at least 2n/3. Significance is modest.
significance.caveat: Modest significance (user may overrule). The conjecture is read as a one-sided O(1) upper bound; the referee showed a two-sided reading is false. Journal versions of the source are unread.
